{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABZSLevQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhC5WVE", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 19, "title": "Schedule VDP2 normal-background VRAM fetches at programmed cycle slots", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17

At main revision `927ad71f238f8ff173f4ac0c3c45ecc4ed71d3da`, VDP2 checks cycle-pattern eligibility but does not execute normal-background reads at their programmed access times.

`src/vdp2/access.rs` checks slot masks, access counts and name-to-character restrictions. However, `DisplayFetch::display_word` in `src/vdp2/fetch.rs:16` reads live VRAM when rendering first requests an address. `Bus::flush_video` renders the elapsed pixel prefix before writes, and HBlank renders the remaining line. No VDP2 fetch deadline participates in `Bus::main_deadline`.

Consequently, data acquisition depends on pixel consumption and rendering flushes rather than the programmed VRAM schedule. A write after the hardware fetch but before first pixel consumption can incorrectly affect that pixel. This consequence follows from code inspection; a new failing timing guest was not executed during planning.

The existing retained-word implementation is valuable: it preserves packed data after first use. Its validation explicitly identifies advance cycle-slot fetching as unfinished. Completing that next step benefits normal-background rendering and CPU/DMA interaction without depending on particular games.

## Expected outcome

Execute normal-background display reads through deterministic hardware-time events. Retain the data acquired at each scheduled access and consume it later during scanout, independently of presentation calls.

Cover NBG0–NBG3 pattern-name and character reads, supported NBG0/NBG1 bitmap reads, and NBG0/NBG1 vertical-cell scroll reads. Respect documented access quantities, bank selection, name/character pipeline restrictions and reduction settings for legal configurations already supported by the renderer.

Use Sega VDP2 User's Manual ST-058-R2 §3.3, figure 3.2, tables 3.2–3.4 and figure 3.5 as the primary contract. Accesses run in T0–T7 order in normal mode and T0–T3 in high-resolution/exclusive modes; sampling must occur through those accesses, rather than an unrestricted render-time read. See the archived [cycle ordering specification](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p03_30.htm), [image access counts and pipeline restrictions](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p03_31.htm), and [vertical-cell access restrictions](https://www.infochunk.com/saturn/segahtml_en/hard/vdp2/hon/p03_32.htm). The original reference is [ST-058-R2](https://github.com/luckyseoul/saturn-docs/blob/main/files/ST-058-R2-060194.pdf).

Integrate display accesses with existing CPU, on-chip DMAC and SCU VRAM transactions. Preserve rotation-bank exclusions and existing rotation rendering. Document any phase convention not established by the primary specifications; do not present an assumed physical latency as measured hardware behavior.

## Context and reproduction

The inspected local revision matches upstream main. Read-only GitHub searches returned no open Issues or PRs, so no duplicate implementation task was found.

Existing evidence establishes first-use retention, not scheduled acquisition:

- `src/vdp2/fetch.rs:67` checks packed-word retention by rendering part of a word, changing VRAM, then rendering the remainder.
- `tests/vdp2_fetch.rs:68` and `scripts/video-transactions.mjs:40` execute the original word-retention guest natively and through production Wasm.
- `docs/hardware-conformance.md:2684` and `docs/validation-issue-17.md:3801` explicitly retain the cycle-slot pipeline gap.

Planning validation actually performed: `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/fixtures/build_vdp2_fetch.py --check` passed; expanded fetch-ROM SHA-256 was `121eb0283aa2e6f0b677bc5a04755efd5e6df2f6b4810cc99d752e0b5ccd727b`. Native hardware tests and browser tests were not rerun during planning. Historical passing records are inherited evidence, not new verification.

Reproduce the missing behavior with a legal cycle pattern and a VRAM write between a scheduled fetch and consumption of its pixels. Include a control with the write before acquisition. Derive expected acquisition times and pixels independently from the manual, not from the emulator's current output.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Implement scheduled normal-background acquisition with retained address/data and pipeline state. Rendering or framebuffer inspection must not initiate missing production display reads, advance hardware time, or change subsequent guest results.
- [ ] Add independent native deadline vectors for each normal-background access class. Check before/at/after acquisition, packed data consumption, subsequent refetch, one/two-word names, supported color formats, scrolling/zoom/reduction, and separate layer/path state. Expected schedules and values must be source-authored with exact manual references.
- [ ] Verify eight-slot and four-slot cycles, split/unsplit banks, legal name-to-character dependencies, vertical-cell ordering, disabled-layer release and rotation-owned bank exclusion. Exercise display/blanking transitions and reset so unfinished fetches cannot leak into a later field or boot. Preserve existing documented behavior for invalid programming configurations without inventing hardware pixel guarantees.
- [ ] Add board-level contention vectors using both SH-2s, on-chip DMAC and all three SCU DMA channels. Verify retained data against actual write-completion boundaries, existing CPU-access restrictions, completion/IRQ order and independent-bank progress. Equal-boundary ordering must be documented and tested consistently.
- [ ] Show identical acquisition traces, guest records and completed pixels across advancement chunks of 1, 3, 17 and 10000 clocks, split at applicable deadlines. Reads must progress without framebuffer requests; repeated debugger inspection must have no effect.
- [ ] Add an original MIT-licensed SH-2 synthetic BIOS or diagnostic disc that programs cycle slots and performs real timed VRAM writes/DMA. Check literal pixels and guest-computed records for writes before acquisition and after acquisition but before consumption. Include source-data and cycle-slot mutations, omitted-write controls, and repeated cold resets. At least one timing assertion must fail against the inherited first-use implementation.
- [ ] Execute the same diagnostic through native `Machine` and rebuilt production Wasm in the existing headless browser suite under `/saturn-rust/`. Assert guest completion, exact framebuffer pixels and Canvas presentation. Host code may provide media and inspect results, but must not write running guest results or draw expected frames.
- [ ] Preserve existing tests and demonstrations, including retained-word tests, raster history, VRAM grants, rotation/window/composition, VDP1, Star Collector completion/restart, Prism Courier, Hardware Lab, audio, both pads, backup retention and browser privacy. Any necessary fixture-timing correction must cite the specification and preserve its substantive assertions.
- [ ] Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native all-target Clippy and Wasm Clippy with `-D warnings`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, all existing and new fixture/media reproduction checks, and the complete `npm run test:browser` without required skips.
- [ ] Update architecture, conformance and validation records with implementation/test links, manual references, fixture provenance/hashes and actual results. Identify remaining limitations and distinguish new evidence from historical results. Correct stale descriptions relevant to this change without changing campaign policy.

This is a partial hardware increment. Rotation-specific acquisition timing, half-line/counter behavior, other video boundaries, remaining CPU/SH7604/68k semantics and timing, board/reset/cache arbitration, SCU/DSP, sound, CD/media/HLE, SMPC and comprehensive integrated acceptance remain mandatory under #17. This task does not establish full hardware completion or demonstrated commercial-game compatibility. Administrative tracker state does not change that scope; do not reopen historical trackers or use umbrella closing keywords.

## Optional validation

Additional source-authored randomized legal cycle patterns, checked against an independent schedule oracle. No personal firmware, commercial discs, physical console, human approval or live Pages inspection is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
